chunks: And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who is overcome by thirst until he fears for his life,
He عليه السلام said: “He may drink in the measure that preserves his remaining strength, and he should not drink until he is fully quenched.”

key_terms.رَمَقَهُ: his remaining life-force or minimal vitality

ai.seo_question: If a fasting person fears death or serious harm from thirst, how much may he drink?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a fasting person who reaches such intense thirst that he fears for his life. He is permitted to drink only enough to preserve himself and avert harm, but not to the point of full satisfaction. It reflects the balance in Shia fiqh between preserving life and maintaining the sanctity of the fast as much as possible.
